items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: Me and Poison Humphrey, we'd be playing together like that, on and off, Em and all of us like that.

ctx.x: Uh, so when did you go into Celestan?

Oh, yeah, I was playing, uh, let me see, then we, Me and Poison Humphrey, we were just working together. Them the fellas I forgot to mention. See, when we'd be living in the field, Me and Poison Humphrey, we'd be playing together like that, on and off, Em and all of us like that. And we decided to make that band strong, you know, just make, organize it like. Yeah. But Sweet Em and Esma, she used it. And the name first was titled from Miss Valente at the paddock. She's the one made Em use that adopted name of the…

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: Then I started working different field work with Poissy Humphrey. And then we started playing and we formally took that outfit and went into Sweet Emma's Band.

ctx.x: Yeah, I don't remember that he told us about that particular group.

Yeah, yeah. I'm trying to think now. Who would I want in with after that? We played around here, 45 and let's see. I was doing field work then and working doing Days of Work. And I think in the year of 1950, Johnny Papacelestand's Jazz Band. I worked in there from 50 to 52. The 90s of Papacelestand, New Orleans Jazz Band. I played with him. When I left in that outfit, we went. Then I started working different field work with Poissy Humphrey. And then we started playing and we formally took that outfit and went…
How many years have you been with Emma now?

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: Remember this, you and Precian, Emma and myself. For sure. Because of piano, a drum, cornet and trombone. We did a television show.

ctx.x: Well, listen. Well, listen. Listen. One thing. You know what I do with him? If the planet player, the center for him player, we got, if he's sick, listen, if the band, we got to start to play. Mean will take it. Listen. He got, we'll take it and play the job. We got a drummer set aside and then there. We gonna play. He got to take his coach. We got a good piano player. All right. We got, do we do, do we do that? Do we play? That's right. If Reed come, let's, we don't worry about Reed. But give it to, if you don't…

Yeah. One Saturday evening. Remember this, you and Precian, Emma and myself. For sure. Because of piano, a drum, cornet and trombone. We did a television show. Played all them numbers. WDSU, a show, played them. Four-piece band. I hope you realize it's, it's, when you take any four people, the chances of them ever getting together is 1-16. Yeah.

You know, you see one thing? You know, we do, this ramp or two parade. But you ain't got to do it because the other boys, you play it. You play it. You know one thing? We was at, uh, at the, at that Venice, the other place there, when we worked there, remember when I got sick, it really went and we, we, we, we, we, we, we, we, we, we, we, we, we was at the, after those. After those. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, that's what, Brennan's, yeah. When people bring one up there, listen so much like that, and Poeusie…

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: Yeah. Mercy's band on Riverside. Yeah. That's one of the old-time drum solos, yeah.

ctx.x: But, I mean, their drum solos would be sort of like those you did with Hammer's band.
Yeah. Mercy's band on Riverside. Yeah. That's one of the old-time drum solos, yeah.
You say you used to play these parades. You use the same drum as you've got here now?
